intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m. Trek through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and glacial moraines while enjoying breathtaking views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli. The trail passes through traditional Gurung villages offering authentic cultural immersion alongside stunning Himalayan scenery.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn to hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises in Nepal. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges including Annapurna South, Annapurna I, and Nilgiri. The 2-hour ascent from Ghorepani is manageable for most fitness levels and rewards trekkers with a panoramic 180-degree mountain vista.

experiences.name: Gurung Village Homestay Experience
experiences.description: Stay overnight in a traditional Gurung village homestay in Ghandruk, one of the largest Gurung settlements in Nepal. Share home-cooked dal bhat, gundruk soup, and raksi (local millet wine) with a local family. Learn about Gurung customs, traditional dress, and the history of Gurkha soldiers. This immersive cultural experience provides authentic insight into Himalayan mountain community life.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trek, a hidden gem offering solitude and raw Himalayan beauty away from the crowded main trails. Trek through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests to High Camp at 3,580m with jaw-dropping close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain) and the Annapurna massif. The 5-7 day route is perfect for trekkers seeking off-the-beaten-path adventure with minimal crowds.

experiences.name: Pokhara Lakeside Nature Walk and Paragliding
experiences.description: Begin with a serene morning walk along the shores of Phewa Lake in Pokhara, the gateway city to Annapurna, with reflections of Machapuchare shimmering on the water. Follow with an exhilarating tandem paragliding flight from Sarangkot hill, soaring over the lake and city with unobstructed views of the entire Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. A perfect active rest day between trekking legs.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange budget taxi or shared shuttle to your accommodation near Pokhara/Annapurna region. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a light late-night snack if available at the hotel or nearby dhaba.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: N/A (in-flight or airport)
meals.dinner: Late-night dal bhat or noodle soup at a local teahouse near the resort (~$3–5)

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy for the next day. Exchange some USD to NPR at the airport for small expenses. Budget taxi from Kathmandu to Pokhara costs ~$20–25 shared, or take a night bus for ~$7–10.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and acclimatize. After a slow morning, explore the immediate surroundings of the resort. Take a short walk along the lakeside (Phewa Lake if near Pokhara) and enjoy fresh mountain air. Visit a local market to stock up on trekking snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) — a short hike or boat ride across Phewa Lake followed by a 30-minute uphill walk. Enjoy panoramic views of the Annapurna range and Pokhara valley. Free entry, boat ride costs ~$2–3.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Lakeside (Bagar) area, browse trekking gear rental shops for any equipment needed. Enjoy sunset over Phewa Lake from the shore.

meals.breakfast: Dal bhat or eggs with tea at resort or local teahouse (~$2–4)
meals.lunch: Momos (dumplings) and butter tea at a lakeside café (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Thali set meal at a local Nepali restaurant in Pokhara (~$4–6)

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to finalize trekking permits: ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) ~$30 and TIMS card ~$20. Both available at the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. Rent trekking poles if needed (~$1–2/day).

day_by_day.morning: Early start — take a local bus or jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (1.5–2 hours, ~$3–5). Begin the Annapurna Circuit/Sanctuary trek. Trek from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (approximately 3–4 hours, moderate trail through terraced fields and small villages).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga to Ulleri (steep stone staircase climb, ~1.5 hours). Enjoy sweeping views of the Annapurna South and Modi Khola valley. Arrive at Ulleri teahouse by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at a budget teahouse in Ulleri (~$3–5/night for a basic dorm or twin room). Explore the small village, interact with locals, and watch the sunset paint the Himalayas golden.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs with tea before departure (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga (~$4–5)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry and rice at Ulleri teahouse (~$4–6)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season — weather should be clear and dry. Wear layers as temperatures drop at altitude. Carry at least 2 liters of water. Total trekking distance today: ~12 km.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early to catch sunrise views of Annapurna South from Ulleri. After breakfast, continue trekking through rhododendron and oak forests toward Ghorepani (approximately 4–5 hours, gradual ascent).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghorepani (2,874m) by early afternoon. Check in to a budget teahouse (~$3–5/night). Rest and acclimatize. Take a short afternoon walk around the village to explore local culture and mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a small cultural gathering or campfire at the teahouse if available. Prepare for the very early morning hike to Poon Hill the next day. Sleep early.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey and tea at Ulleri teahouse (~$3–4)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a trail teahouse (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with vegetable curry at Ghorepani teahouse (~$5–7)

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani sits at 2,874m — stay hydrated and avoid alcohol to prevent altitude sickness. Total trekking distance today: ~10 km. Set alarm for 04:30 for next morning's Poon Hill hike.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) — depart at 04:30–05:00 (1 hour uphill hike). Witness one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises in the world with 360° views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna range, and Machhapuchhre. Entry fee ~$2. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani through dense rhododendron forest (approximately 4–5 hours). Enjoy diverse flora and occasional wildlife sightings. Arrive at Tadapani teahouse by afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse, dry any wet gear, and journal about the day's highlights. Enjoy clear evening views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain).

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and tea after returning from Poon Hill (~$3–4)
meals.lunch: Vegetable soup and chapati at a trail teahouse (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Pasta or dal bhat at Tadapani teahouse (~$4–6)

day_by_day.notes: This is one of the most memorable days of the trek. Bring a warm jacket for the Poon Hill summit — temperatures can be near freezing before sunrise. Total trekking distance today: ~14 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (approximately 4–5 hours). The trail descends steeply then climbs again through beautiful terraced hillsides. Chhomrong is the gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary and offers stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong (2,170m). Check in to a budget teahouse (~$3–5). Explore the village, visit the local gompa (monastery), and chat with fellow trekkers about trail conditions ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the warm community atmosphere of Chhomrong. Watch the last light fade on Annapurna South from the village viewpoint. Plan the route for the next few days.

meals.breakfast: Eggs on toast and tea at Tadapani teahouse (~$3–4)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a teahouse mid-trail (~$4–5)
meals.dinner: Garlic soup (great for altitude) and vegetable curry at Chhomrong teahouse (~$5–7)

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is highly recommended at altitude — locals swear by it for acclimatization. Total trekking distance today: ~11 km. Refill water bottles and carry extra snacks for the next section.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong to Himalaya Hotel (approximately 5–6 hours). The trail descends to Sinuwa, then follows the Modi Khola river through bamboo and rhododendron forests. The landscape becomes increasingly dramatic and remote.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (2,920m) by mid-afternoon. This is a good acclimatization stop before heading higher. Rest, hydrate, and enjoy the increasingly dramatic canyon views.
day_by_day.evening: Cozy evening at the teahouse. The atmosphere becomes more intimate as fewer teahouses exist at this altitude. Stargaze from the trail — October skies are exceptionally clear.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and boiled eggs at Chhomrong teahouse (~$3–4)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at Sinuwa teahouse (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with lentil soup at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (~$5–7)

day_by_day.notes: Water purification tablets or a filter are essential beyond this point — buy purified water (~$1–2/bottle) or treat your own. Total trekking distance today: ~12 km. Temperature drops significantly at night.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) via Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC). Depart early (06:00). Trek through Deurali and MBC (3,700m), then continue the final push to ABC (4,130m) — total approximately 6–7 hours of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Annapurna Base Camp! You are now surrounded by a natural amphitheater of Himalayan giants: Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, Hiunchuli, and Gangapurna. Spend the afternoon soaking in this awe-inspiring 360° panorama.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset turn the surrounding peaks from gold to pink to purple — a truly unforgettable experience. Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers over hot drinks. Sleep at ABC teahouse (~$5–8/night).

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and tea before departure (~$3–4)
meals.lunch: Quick snack and energy bars on the trail (carry from below)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at ABC teahouse (~$6–8)

day_by_day.notes: This is the highest point of the trek at 4,130m. Signs of altitude sickness include headache, nausea, and dizziness — descend immediately if symptoms worsen. Drink 3–4 liters of water. Temperatures at night can drop to -10°C. Total trekking distance today: ~13 km.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for the magical ABC sunrise — watch the first rays illuminate Annapurna I and Machhapuchhre in brilliant orange and gold. This is the highlight of the entire trek. Take plenty of photos and absorb the moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC back to Bamboo teahouse (approximately 5–6 hours descending). The return journey is faster but hard on the knees. Enjoy different perspectives of the landscape on the way down.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Bamboo teahouse (~$3–5/night). Enjoy the warmer temperatures and thicker air at lower altitude. Soak tired feet and relax.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and biscuits at ABC before sunrise, then full breakfast after (~$4–5)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Himalaya Hotel teahouse on descent (~$4–6)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry and rice at Bamboo teahouse (~$4–6)

day_by_day.notes: Descending is harder on knees than ascending — trekking poles are very helpful today. Pace yourself and take breaks. Total trekking distance today: ~16 km. You've conquered the Annapurna Sanctuary!

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Bamboo to Jhinu Danda (approximately 4–5 hours). Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs along the Modi Khola river — a perfect reward for tired trekking legs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda (~$3 entry). Soak in the geothermal pools beside the rushing river surrounded by jungle. This is one of the most relaxing experiences on the entire trek.
day_by_day.evening: Stay overnight at a budget teahouse in Jhinu Danda (~$3–5). Enjoy the warm, celebratory atmosphere — many trekkers celebrate completing the Sanctuary trek here.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes and tea at Bamboo teahouse (~$3–4)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup mid-trail (~$3–4)
meals.dinner: Special celebration dinner — try apple pie (famous in the region) and dal bhat (~$5–7)

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs are busiest in late afternoon — arrive early for a quieter experience. The pools are naturally heated and sit right beside the river. Total trekking distance today: ~10 km.

day_by_day.morning: Final trekking day — trek from Jhinu Danda back to Nayapul (approximately 4–5 hours through Chhomrong and lower trail sections). Reflect on the incredible journey through the Annapurna region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul and catch a local bus or jeep back to Pokhara (1.5–2 hours, ~$3–5). Check back in to Aegean Bliss Resort or a budget guesthouse in Pokhara. Take a long shower — the first proper one in days!
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the trek with a lakeside dinner in Pokhara. Explore the Lakeside area, browse souvenir shops for budget gifts, and enjoy a well-deserved cold drink.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and eggs at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~$3–4)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a trail teahouse in Chhomrong (~$4–5)
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a Lakeside restaurant in Pokhara (~$5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Total trekking distance today: ~12 km. You've completed approximately 100+ km of trekking over 9 days! Return trekking permits/gear rentals and get a receipt. Visit a pharmacy if you have any minor injuries or blisters.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in, then take a gentle morning boat ride on Phewa Lake (~$5–8/hour for a rowboat). The reflections of Machhapuchhre on the calm lake are stunning on clear October mornings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (~$7 entry) — fascinating exhibits on Himalayan mountaineering history, local culture, and the geology of the Annapurna region. Very relevant after your trek.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Nepali cultural show at a local restaurant (some offer free shows with dinner). Browse the Lakeside market for handmade crafts, pashmina scarves, and thangka paintings at budget prices.

meals.breakfast: Full Nepali breakfast with tea at a lakeside café (~$3–5)
meals.lunch: Buff momos (buffalo dumplings) and lassi at a local restaurant (~$4–6)
meals.dinner: Newari set meal with cultural show at a traditional restaurant (~$6–9)

day_by_day.notes: This is a great day to get a budget massage (~$10–15/hour) to help muscles recover. Also consider visiting a local pharmacy for any post-trek ailments. Check weather forecasts for remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Bindhyabasini Temple — a sacred hilltop Hindu temple with excellent views of the Annapurna range and the city. Free entry, small donation appreciated. Witness morning puja (prayer rituals).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or shared taxi to Sarangkot viewpoint (~$2–3 each way) for panoramic Himalayan views including Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, and Manaslu. Alternatively, hike up (1.5 hours) for free. Watch paragliders launch from the hill (~$80–100 if you want to try — splurge option).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Pokhara — stroll along the entire Lakeside promenade, enjoy a sunset dinner by the lake, and pick up any last-minute souvenirs. Pack bags for the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with butter and tea near Bindhyabasini Temple (~$2–3)
meals.lunch: Fried rice and vegetable curry at a Sarangkot teahouse (~$4–5)
meals.dinner: Farewell lakeside dinner — try the local fish (Pokhara is known for fresh lake fish) (~$6–9)

day_by_day.notes: October weather in Pokhara is typically clear and mild (~18–25°C during the day). Confirm your return transport to Kathmandu for tomorrow — tourist bus (~$10–12) or flight (~$80–100). Book in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise views from the resort or lakeside. Take a last walk along Phewa Lake shore and say goodbye to the Annapurna range. Check out of accommodation and arrange transport to Kathmandu (tourist bus: ~$10–12, departs ~07:00–08:00, 6–7 hours; or 25-minute flight ~$80–100).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kathmandu. If time permits before your onward flight, visit the historic Thamel district for last-minute souvenir shopping. Explore Boudhanath Stupa or Pashupatinath Temple if time allows (~$3–5 entry for foreigners).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Tribhuvan International Airport for departure. Enjoy a final plate of momos or dal bhat at an airport restaurant. Reflect on an incredible 14-day budget adventure through the Annapurna region of Nepal.

meals.breakfast: Final Nepali breakfast at resort before checkout (~$3–5)
meals.lunch: Quick dal bhat or noodles on the road or in Kathmandu (~$3–5)
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or Thamel farewell meal — try chicken sekuwa (grilled chicken) (~$5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departure. Nepal airport tax is included in most tickets but confirm. Total estimated budget for the 14-day trip (excluding flights): $350–500 USD covering accommodation, meals, permits, transport, and activities — a very achievable budget for the Annapurna region.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Complete immigration and customs, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged transfer to your accommodation. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, Annapurna. Freshen up and get a good night's rest before the adventure begins.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival if available

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance. Keep essentials like snacks and water in your carry-on. Exchange some currency (NPR) at the airport or use an ATM. Confirm resort check-in details ahead of time since arrival is late night.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning getting oriented — explore the resort grounds, review your trek gear, and consult with the resort's trekking desk or local guide about the upcoming days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle introductory walk around the nearby village of Pokhara or the lakeside area (if the resort is near Phewa Lake). Visit the Bindhyabasini Temple and stroll through the old bazaar to soak in local culture and pick up any last-minute trekking supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Lakeside (Baidam) area for a relaxed dinner with views of Phewa Lake. Explore the vibrant street scene, browse local handicraft shops, and enjoy the laid-back mountain-town atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — try local items like sel roti, eggs, and Nepali tea
meals.lunch: Momos and thukpa (noodle soup) at a local teahouse near the bazaar — budget NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dal bhat set meal or wood-fired pizza at a mid-range lakeside restaurant like Caffe Concerto or Moondance Restaurant — budget NPR 800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Stay hydrated and avoid overexertion today. Begin acclimatization by keeping activity light. Purchase a Nepal SIM card (NTC or Ncell) for connectivity. Confirm trekking permits if not already arranged.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat ride on Phewa Lake to the Tal Barahi Temple (island temple) — a peaceful and scenic experience. Watch the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) peaks reflect on the lake at sunrise. Return by 8:00 AM for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara — one of Asia's best mountaineering museums. Learn about Himalayan expeditions, local culture, and the history of the Annapurna range. Spend 2–3 hours exploring.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Nepali cultural show featuring Gurung and Tharu dances at a local cultural center. Afterward, enjoy dinner at a rooftop restaurant with Himalayan views.

meals.breakfast: Eggs, toast, porridge, and fresh juice at the resort or a nearby café
meals.lunch: Nepali thali at a local restaurant near the museum — budget NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Grilled chicken or vegetable curry with rice at a rooftop restaurant in Lakeside — budget NPR 900–1,300

day_by_day.notes: Boat rides on Phewa Lake cost approximately NPR 500–800 per hour. Museum entry is around NPR 300 for foreigners. October is peak trekking season — book guides and permits early.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a local bus to Nayapul (about 1.5 hours from Pokhara). Begin the classic Annapurna Circuit or Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trail. Trek from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (approximately 3–4 hours, 1,540m elevation) through terraced fields and rhododendron forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking or rest at Tikhedhunga. Explore the charming village, interact with locals, and watch the Bhurungdi Khola river rushing below. Take short nature walks around the village area.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a teahouse in Tikhedhunga. Enjoy the warm hospitality of a family-run lodge. Sit around the communal dining area, meet fellow trekkers, and share stories.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure — eggs, toast, and tea
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse in Hile or along the trail — budget NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dal bhat (unlimited refills) at your teahouse in Tikhedhunga — budget NPR 500–700 (often included in teahouse package)

day_by_day.notes: Carry TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) — obtain these in Pokhara before departure (approx. NPR 2,000 + NPR 3,000 for foreigners). Pack light but include rain gear, layers, and a headlamp. October weather is generally clear and cool — ideal for trekking.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tikhedhunga to Ghorepani (approximately 5–6 hours, 2,860m elevation). The trail climbs steeply through dense rhododendron and oak forests. The ascent is challenging but rewarding with spectacular views emerging above the treeline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghorepani by early afternoon. Check in to a mid-range teahouse. Rest, rehydrate, and acclimatize. Take a short exploratory walk around the village and visit the small local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges from Ghorepani village. Gather in the teahouse dining room for warmth, hot drinks, and good conversation with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Porridge, eggs, and hot tea at Tikhedhunga teahouse
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a trail teahouse — vegetable soup and bread — budget NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta with garlic soup at Ghorepani teahouse — budget NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: The climb to Ghorepani is one of the steeper sections — take it slow and rest frequently. Altitude increases significantly today. Watch for signs of altitude sickness: headache, nausea, dizziness. Drink 3–4 liters of water throughout the day. Teahouse accommodation in Ghorepani costs approximately NPR 300–600 per night.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at 4:30 AM to hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) — approximately 45 minutes from Ghorepani. Witness one of Nepal's most iconic sunrises with a 360-degree panorama of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre, Annapurna I, II, III, and IV. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (approximately 4–5 hours, 2,630m) through magnificent rhododendron forests — the largest in Nepal. The trail offers continuous mountain views and diverse birdlife including Himalayan monals.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Tadapani and settle into a teahouse. Enjoy the quieter, less-crowded atmosphere compared to Ghorepani. Watch the alpenglow on Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, boiled eggs, and ginger tea after returning from Poon Hill
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a trail teahouse — budget NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry, rice, and lentil soup at Tadapani teahouse — budget NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee is NPR 100. Bring a warm jacket, gloves, and a headlamp for the pre-dawn hike. The sunrise view is considered one of the best in the Himalayas — absolutely unmissable. Camera batteries drain faster in the cold — keep them warm in your inner pocket.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (approximately 4–5 hours, 2,170m). The trail descends through forests and crosses the Modi Khola river before a steep climb to Chhomrong — the last major village before the Annapurna Sanctuary. Enjoy stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chhomrong village — a traditional Gurung settlement with stone-paved paths, terraced fields, and warm locals. Visit the small Chhomrong Khola viewpoint and rest your legs. The village has better facilities including hot showers and charging points.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the terrace of your teahouse with views of the mountains. The clear October skies make for brilliant stargazing after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey and hot chocolate at Tadapani teahouse
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a teahouse in Sinuwa or along the trail
meals.dinner: Apple pie (a Chhomrong specialty), soup, and a main course at a mid-range teahouse — budget NPR 700–1,000

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong is a good place to stock up on snacks, water purification tablets, and any gear you may need. Hot showers are available for an extra NPR 200–300. The apple products (pie, juice, raksi) in this region are locally made and delicious.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong to Dovan (approximately 5–6 hours, 2,600m) via Sinuwa and Bamboo. The trail enters the Annapurna Sanctuary, descending into bamboo and rhododendron forests. Watch for wildlife including Himalayan tahr, langur monkeys, and colorful pheasants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Dovan and rest. The landscape becomes more dramatic as the valley narrows. Explore the immediate surroundings and listen to the roar of mountain streams.
day_by_day.evening: The teahouse options are limited here but cozy. Enjoy a simple but satisfying dinner and early bedtime to prepare for tomorrow's long push toward base camp.

meals.breakfast: Eggs, toast, and tea at Chhomrong teahouse
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or quick stop at Bamboo teahouse — noodle soup or fried rice
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at Dovan teahouse — budget NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: The trail through the bamboo forest can be slippery — use trekking poles. This section is known for occasional wildlife sightings. Keep noise low and move quietly. The trail is well-marked but can be narrow in places. Acclimatization is important — do not rush.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) (approximately 5–6 hours, 3,700m) via Himalaya Hotel and Annapurna Base Camp approach trail. The scenery becomes increasingly dramatic with glacial moraines and towering peaks closing in on all sides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at MBC and rest. The sacred Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Peak, 6,993m) towers directly above. Spend time acclimatizing — short walks around the camp area. The views are extraordinary and surreal.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset paint Machhapuchhre, Annapurna South, and Hiunchuli in shades of gold and pink. The temperature drops sharply — layer up. Enjoy a warm meal and get to bed early.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and hot lemon tea at Dovan
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and bread at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — garlic helps with acclimatization
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at MBC teahouse — budget NPR 700–900 (prices increase at altitude)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness risk increases significantly above 3,000m. Symptoms include headache, loss of appetite, and fatigue. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol. Teahouse prices are higher at altitude due to supply difficulties — budget accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Very early start (5:00 AM) to trek from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) (approximately 1.5–2 hours, 4,130m). Arrive at ABC for the most spectacular sunrise of the trip — surrounded by a full amphitheater of Himalayan giants including Annapurna I (8,091m), the 10th highest peak in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning and early afternoon at ABC soaking in the views, taking photos, and celebrating the achievement. Explore the glacier viewpoints and memorial plaques. Begin the descent back to MBC and continue to Deurali or Bamboo (approximately 3–4 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Settle in at a lower-altitude teahouse. The descent brings immediate relief from altitude effects. Enjoy a celebratory dinner and reflect on the incredible achievement.

meals.breakfast: Light snack before sunrise hike — energy bars and hot tea at MBC
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at ABC or on descent — budget NPR 800–1,100
meals.dinner: Celebratory dal bhat with extra helpings at Deurali or Bamboo teahouse — budget NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the entire trip. October provides the clearest views of the season. The full Annapurna Sanctuary amphitheater includes Annapurna I, II, III, IV, South, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, Khangsar Kang, and Machhapuchhre. Take your time here — you have earned it. Descend the same day to avoid prolonged altitude exposure.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Bamboo/Deurali back through Chhomrong to Jhinu Danda (approximately 5–6 hours, 1,780m). The descent is rapid and the air noticeably thicker and warmer as you lose altitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reward yourself with a soak in the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda — a perfect remedy for tired trekking legs. The hot springs are set alongside the Modi Khola river in a beautiful natural setting.
day_by_day.evening: Relax in the warm, comfortable teahouses of Jhinu Danda. The lower altitude means better sleep and more energy. Celebrate the completion of the Annapurna Sanctuary trek.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and porridge at your teahouse before descent
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or fried noodles at Chhomrong on the way down
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry, rice, and fresh local vegetables at Jhinu Danda — budget NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: Hot springs entry at Jhinu Danda costs approximately NPR 200–300. Bring a towel and change of clothes. The springs are open morning to evening. This is one of the most satisfying moments of the trek — thoroughly deserved. The descent from ABC to Jhinu in one day is long but very doable.

day_by_day.morning: Final trekking day — hike from Jhinu Danda to Nayapul (approximately 4–5 hours) via Kimche and Birethanti. The trail passes through terraced rice paddies, suspension bridges, and charming Gurung villages. A gentle and nostalgic final walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch a local bus or pre-arranged vehicle from Nayapul back to Pokhara (approximately 1.5 hours). Check back in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Shower, do laundry, and decompress after 9 days of trekking.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a well-deserved celebration dinner in Pokhara's Lakeside area. Enjoy the lively atmosphere, good food, and the satisfaction of completing one of the world's great treks.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes and hot chocolate at Jhinu Danda teahouse
meals.lunch: Final trail meal — dal bhat or momo at Birethanti teahouse
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at a mid-range Lakeside restaurant — try Everest Steak House or Moondance — budget NPR 1,200–1,800

day_by_day.notes: Nayapul to Pokhara bus costs approximately NPR 200–300. Taxi costs NPR 2,000–3,000. Celebrate your achievement — you have trekked to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m! Consider a traditional Nepali massage in Pokhara to soothe sore muscles (NPR 1,000–1,500 for 60 minutes).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast, and get a full-body massage or yoga session. Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) on the hilltop south of Phewa Lake — a 30-minute hike or short drive with panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave near the Davis Falls — a sacred Hindu cave with natural rock formations and underground streams. Explore the Davis Falls (Patale Chhango) — a dramatic waterfall that disappears underground. Browse the Tibetan refugee camp and market for handmade crafts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset paragliding over Pokhara Valley and Phewa Lake — one of the world's top paragliding destinations. Tandem flights with certified operators cost approximately USD 80–100 and last 30–45 minutes. Alternatively, watch the sunset from the lakeside promenade.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — eggs Benedict, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Thakali set meal (a regional Nepali specialty) at a local restaurant — budget NPR 600–900
meals.dinner: Grilled fish from Phewa Lake or wood-fired pizza at a lakeside restaurant — budget NPR 1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding season in October is excellent — calm winds and clear skies. Book with reputable operators like Sunrise Paragliding or Blue Sky Paragliding. World Peace Pagoda hike is approximately 45 minutes each way and offers some of the best views in Pokhara. Carry your passport for cave and falls entry.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Pokhara — enjoy a sunrise boat ride on Phewa Lake one last time. Visit the Barahi Temple island. Reflect on the incredible 14-day journey. After breakfast, pack your bags and prepare for departure. Last-minute souvenir shopping in the Lakeside bazaar — pashmina scarves, Thangka paintings, trekking gear, and local spices make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange transfer to Pokhara Regional Airport for a short domestic flight back to Kathmandu (30 minutes, approximately USD 100–130) or take the tourist bus (approximately 6–7 hours, NPR 800–1,200). If flying, arrive in Kathmandu with time to visit Thamel for final shopping or a farewell meal.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Kathmandu or Pokhara depending on your departure schedule. Celebrate the entire journey with a special meal. Prepare for your international departure — ensure you have all documents, permits returned, and souvenirs packed within customs limits.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — full spread with local and continental options
meals.lunch: Quick but delicious meal at a Thamel restaurant in Kathmandu — try Thamel House Restaurant for authentic Nepali cuisine — budget NPR 1,000–1,500
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Thamel — Nepali set menu with cultural performances — budget NPR 1,500–2,500

day_by_day.notes: Domestic flights from Pokhara to Kathmandu can be delayed — allow extra buffer time before international connections. Keep trekking permits and ACAP cards as souvenirs. Nepal's customs allow export of handicrafts under NPR 25,000 without documentation. Ensure international flight check-in is completed online. This concludes an extraordinary 14-day Annapurna adventure — a journey of a lifetime.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn to hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises in Nepal. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges including Annapurna South, Annapurna I, and Nilgiri. The 2-hour ascent from Ghorepani is manageable for most fitness levels and rewards trekkers with a panoramic 180-degree mountain vista.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30. Transfer from Tribhuvan International Airport to your luxury accommodation in the Annapurna region via private chauffeured vehicle. Check-in and settle into your Beachfront suite at Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in-flight or transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night welcome drink and light refreshments arranged by the resort upon arrival. Meet your dedicated concierge who will brief you on the 14-day journey ahead. Retire early to rest and acclimatize.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or pre-departure meal
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter and herbal teas prepared by the resort chef upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — no sightseeing scheduled. Ensure you stay hydrated after the flight. The resort will have a warm welcome kit including altitude acclimatization supplements, organic teas, and a personalized itinerary booklet waiting in your suite.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late morning start to recover from travel. Enjoy a gourmet Nepali and continental breakfast at the resort's panoramic dining terrace overlooking the Annapurna massif. Followed by a private orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby village of Pokhara lakeside, introducing you to local flora, culture, and the stunning Phewa Lake views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided boat ride on Phewa Lake in a luxury wooden vessel. Visit the iconic Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of the lake. Stroll the serene lakeside promenade with your guide, learning about the Annapurna Conservation Area. Enjoy a curated photography session with the Annapurna range as backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort terrace with unobstructed Himalayan views. Private candlelit dinner at the resort's signature restaurant featuring a curated menu of Newari and contemporary Nepali cuisine paired with fine wines.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet Nepali and continental breakfast at the resort terrace — fresh sel roti, eggs benedict, seasonal fruits, and Himalayan herbal teas
meals.lunch: Light lakeside lunch at a premium Pokhara restaurant — grilled trout, Nepali thali, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — Newari-inspired tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is an acclimatization and orientation day. Keep activities gentle. Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol in large quantities to help your body adjust to the altitude. Your concierge will confirm all trekking gear and equipment for upcoming days.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private yoga and meditation session on the resort's outdoor deck with a certified Himalayan yoga instructor, set against the backdrop of the Annapurna and Machapuchare peaks. Follow with a nutritious power breakfast designed by the resort's nutritionist to fuel upcoming treks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided hike to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) perched at 1,100m above Pokhara. The hike takes approximately 1.5–2 hours through lush subtropical forest. Enjoy sweeping 360-degree views of the Annapurna range, Dhaulagiri, Manaslu, and Phewa Lake from the summit. A private picnic lunch with gourmet hamper is set up at the pagoda viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a rejuvenating Himalayan stone massage at the resort's luxury spa. Evening briefing with your lead trekking guide over a premium dinner to review the upcoming Annapurna Circuit route, gear check, and logistics.

meals.breakfast: High-energy trekker's breakfast — granola, poached eggs, avocado toast, fresh fruit bowls, and green smoothies
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic hamper at World Peace Pagoda — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, seasonal fruits, and premium bottled water
meals.dinner: Fine dining at resort — Himalayan herb-crusted lamb, saffron rice, roasted vegetables, and decadent dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Gear check is essential this evening. Ensure trekking poles, boots, layered clothing, and altitude medication (Diamox if prescribed) are all ready. October is peak trekking season — expect clear skies and stunning visibility.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Pokhara by private luxury vehicle to Nayapul (approximately 1.5 hours). Begin the iconic Annapurna Circuit trek with your private guide and personal porter. Trek through terraced rice fields, rhododendron forests, and traditional Gurung villages from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (approximately 4–5 hours, 1,540m elevation).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through the Modi Khola river valley, passing through the charming village of Birethanti. Arrive at Tikhedhunga and check into a premium pre-booked teahouse with private rooms and ensuite facilities. Freshen up and explore the local village with your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views over the Annapurna foothills from the teahouse terrace. Private chef-prepared dinner at the teahouse featuring locally sourced dal bhat, vegetable curries, and fresh mountain bread. Early bedtime to prepare for the ascent tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — eggs to order, toast, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at a premium teahouse in Birethanti — vegetable soup, momos, and herbal tea
meals.dinner: Authentic Nepali dal bhat feast at Tikhedhunga teahouse, prepared by private cook — lentil soup, seasonal vegetables, pickles, and rice

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today: approximately 11 km. Elevation gain: ~600m. Pace is moderate. Your personal porter will carry all heavy gear. Carry only a light daypack with water, snacks, sunscreen, and a rain jacket. October weather is typically clear and dry — perfect trekking conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Rise at 05:30 for an early breakfast and begin the famous stone staircase ascent from Tikhedhunga to Ulleri (1,960m) — a challenging but rewarding climb of approximately 3,000 stone steps through dense forest. Continue trekking through Banthanti and Nangethanti to reach Ghorepani (2,860m) by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghorepani and check into a premium teahouse with mountain views. Rest and acclimatize at altitude. Optional gentle afternoon walk to explore the village and surrounding rhododendron forest — the largest rhododendron forest in Nepal. Acclimatization exercises with your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Hot shower and relaxation at the teahouse. Sunset views over Dhaulagiri and the Annapurna South face from Ghorepani village. Private dinner featuring warming Nepali soups, pasta, and hot chocolate. Early bedtime — tomorrow's Poon Hill sunrise hike requires a 04:00 wake-up call.

meals.breakfast: Early energy breakfast at Tikhedhunga — porridge, boiled eggs, toast with honey, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Nangethanti — noodle soup, spring rolls, and fresh lemon tea
meals.dinner: Warming dinner at Ghorepani premium teahouse — garlic soup, spaghetti bolognese, apple pie, and hot chocolate

day_by_day.notes: Today is the most physically demanding day so far — the Ulleri stone staircase is steep and long. Take your time, rest frequently, and stay hydrated. Elevation tonight is 2,860m — some guests may feel mild altitude effects. Inform your guide immediately of any symptoms. Set your alarm for 04:00 AM for Poon Hill tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 04:00 AM for the iconic Poon Hill Sunrise Hike. Trek by headlamp through the dark rhododendron forest to reach Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m (approximately 45–60 minutes). Witness one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises on Earth — the golden light illuminating Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machapuchare (Fishtail), and dozens of other peaks. Private photography session with your guide. Return to Ghorepani for a hot breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: After breakfast, trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (2,610m) via Deurali Pass — a beautiful ridge walk through ancient rhododendron and oak forests with continuous panoramic mountain views (approximately 4–5 hours). Arrive at Tadapani and check into premium teahouse accommodations.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and enjoy the tranquil mountain atmosphere at Tadapani. Sundowner drinks on the teahouse terrace overlooking Machapuchare. Private dinner with your guide — reflect on the day's highlights and discuss tomorrow's route to Chomrong.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike: energy bars and thermos of hot ginger tea at 04:00 AM. Post-hike full breakfast at Ghorepani — pancakes, eggs, toast, porridge, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch prepared by teahouse — sandwiches, energy bars, nuts, and fruit
meals.dinner: Hearty dinner at Tadapani teahouse — vegetable curry, rice, lentil soup, and warm apple cider

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the absolute highlight of the first week — do not miss it regardless of weather. In October, skies are almost always crystal clear at dawn. Dress in warm layers as temperatures at 3,210m before sunrise can drop to -5°C. Your guide will carry a thermos of hot tea for the summit.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga and stretching session on the teahouse terrace at Tadapani with your guide leading breathing exercises adapted for altitude. After breakfast, begin the descent through magnificent rhododendron and bamboo forest toward Chomrong (2,170m) — gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary. Trek duration approximately 4–5 hours with stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chomrong — a beautiful Gurung village perched on a hillside. Check into a premium teahouse with private room and mountain views. Afternoon exploration of Chomrong village with your guide — visit the local school, monastery, and interact with Gurung families. Learn about the indigenous Gurung culture and their deep connection to the Himalayas.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at the teahouse with panoramic views of the Annapurna Sanctuary entrance. Private cultural dinner featuring traditional Gurung cuisine — gundruk (fermented greens), dhido (buckwheat porridge), and local raksi (millet wine) for those who wish. Stargazing session with your guide — at this altitude and away from city lights, the Milky Way is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Nutritious breakfast at Tadapani — muesli, boiled eggs, toast with local honey, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch en route — tomato soup, cheese sandwich, and lemon tea
meals.dinner: Traditional Gurung cultural dinner at Chomrong premium teahouse — gundruk soup, dhido, seasonal vegetables, and local herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Rest day rhythm — today's trek is moderate and allows time to appreciate the culture and scenery. Chomrong is a pivotal staging point for the Annapurna Base Camp route. Your guide will discuss the option to extend toward ABC tomorrow if you feel acclimatized and energetic. Ensure all gear is ready for higher altitude tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: After an early breakfast, descend the famous Chomrong stone staircase and begin trekking through the dramatic Chomrong Khola valley toward Sinuwa (2,340m) and then Bamboo (2,310m). Trek through dense bamboo and rhododendron forest — a habitat for Himalayan black bears, red pandas, and diverse birdlife. Your naturalist guide will identify wildlife and flora along the route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Bamboo through Doban to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m). The trail follows the Modi Khola river through increasingly dramatic gorge scenery with towering walls of rock and ice on either side. Arrive at Himalaya Hotel teahouse and check in. The landscape becomes increasingly alpine and awe-inspiring.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and acclimatize at Himalaya Hotel. The temperature drops noticeably at this altitude. Warm up with hot soups and herbal teas. Private dinner prepared by the teahouse cook. Your guide will conduct a detailed briefing on tomorrow's approach to Annapurna Base Camp — the crown jewel of the trek.

meals.breakfast: High-energy breakfast at Chomrong — egg fried rice, toast, fresh fruit, and ginger lemon honey tea
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch at Bamboo teahouse — noodle soup, boiled eggs, and energy bars
meals.dinner: Warming dinner at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — garlic soup (altitude remedy), pasta, vegetable stir-fry, and hot chocolate

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is highly recommended at altitude — it is a traditional Nepali remedy believed to help with acclimatization. Drink minimum 3–4 liters of water today. Altitude tonight is approximately 2,920m. Watch for any signs of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS): headache, nausea, dizziness. Inform your guide immediately if symptoms arise.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Himalaya Hotel. Trek through Deurali (3,230m) and into the sacred Annapurna Sanctuary — a vast glacial amphitheater ringed by some of the world's highest peaks. The landscape transforms dramatically into a high-alpine glacial environment. Trek to Machapuchare Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m — a stunning viewpoint with direct views of the sacred Fishtail Mountain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the final push from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — the ultimate destination of this trek. Arrive to the breathtaking 360-degree panorama of Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, and the iconic Machapuchare. Check into the premium teahouse at ABC. Spend the afternoon absorbing the extraordinary high-altitude environment.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Annapurna Base Camp — one of the most magnificent spectacles on Earth as the last golden light turns the surrounding 7,000m and 8,000m peaks pink and crimson. Private champagne toast at 4,130m to celebrate reaching the base camp. Warm dinner and early rest — temperatures at night can drop to -10°C or below.

meals.breakfast: Power breakfast at Himalaya Hotel — porridge with honey and nuts, boiled eggs, toast, and hot tea
meals.lunch: Hot soup and snacks at Machapuchare Base Camp teahouse — tomato soup, crackers, and energy bars
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at ABC teahouse — dal bhat, vegetable curry, and a special dessert. Private champagne or sparkling water toast at sunset

day_by_day.notes: Reaching ABC at 4,130m is a significant achievement. This is the highest point of the trek. Take it very slowly on the ascent from MBC — altitude affects everyone differently. Your guide is trained in wilderness first aid and carries emergency oxygen. The premium champagne for the sunset toast will be carried up by your personal porter as a special surprise arranged by the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for the Annapurna Base Camp sunrise — arguably the most dramatic mountain sunrise experience in the world as the first light sets the entire glacial amphitheater ablaze in gold and pink. Spend the morning exploring the base camp area, visiting the memorial chortens, and absorbing the profound silence and scale of the Himalayan giants surrounding you.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC back toward Bamboo (2,310m) — a long but rewarding descent retracing the route through MBC, Deurali, and Himalaya Hotel. The descent is significantly easier than the ascent and the changing perspectives of the mountains are equally stunning. Arrive at Bamboo teahouse for the night.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at Bamboo teahouse — the hardest part of the trek is complete. Your guide will share stories of the Annapurna Sanctuary and its spiritual significance to the Gurung people. Rest well — your body will appreciate the lower altitude.

meals.breakfast: Early sunrise breakfast at ABC — porridge, boiled eggs, toast, and hot ginger tea
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at Himalaya Hotel — noodle soup, spring rolls, and lemon tea
meals.dinner: Hearty celebratory dinner at Bamboo teahouse — pasta, vegetable curry, rice pudding, and hot chocolate

day_by_day.notes: Descending from 4,130m to 2,310m in one day is a long journey — approximately 7–8 hours of trekking. However, most guests feel energized by the lower altitude. Trekking poles are essential for the steep descents. Your knees will thank you for taking it slowly on the downhill sections.

day_by_day.morning: After a well-deserved rest, trek from Bamboo back up to Chomrong (2,170m) via Sinuwa. The ascent up the Chomrong stone staircase is challenging but brief. Arrive at Chomrong and enjoy a late morning rest with panoramic views. Optional visit to the Chomrong monastery for a private blessing ceremony arranged by your guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Chomrong to Jhinu Danda (1,760m) — a short but beautiful trail descending through terraced fields and traditional villages. The highlight of the afternoon: a private soak in the famous Jhinu Danda natural hot springs beside the Modi Khola river — the perfect reward after days of high-altitude trekking. Private towels, robes, and refreshments arranged by your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Jhinu Danda premium teahouse. Relaxed dinner featuring locally caught river fish, seasonal vegetables, and warming herbal teas. Reflect on the extraordinary week of trekking with your guide over a final trail dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Bamboo teahouse — muesli, eggs, toast, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Lunch at Chomrong teahouse — dal soup, rice, and fresh lemon tea
meals.dinner: Riverside dinner at Jhinu Danda — fresh river trout, roasted vegetables, rice, and herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs are a legendary highlight for trekkers completing the ABC route. The natural thermal springs are set in a beautiful gorge beside the river. Your guide will arrange a private early-morning slot if you prefer a quieter experience. This is one of the most relaxing and rewarding moments of the entire trip.

day_by_day.morning: Optional early morning hot springs soak before breakfast. Trek from Jhinu Danda to Nayapul (approximately 3–4 hours) through beautiful lower-altitude forest and traditional Gurung and Magar villages. Enjoy the warmer temperatures and lush subtropical vegetation as you descend. Private vehicle waiting at Nayapul for the transfer back to Pokhara.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Pokhara and check back into Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the luxury of your Beachfront suite — hot shower, fresh linens, and resort amenities after 9 days of trekking. Afternoon at leisure — optional Phewa Lake kayaking, resort swimming pool, or simply relaxing on your private terrace with Himalayan views.
day_by_day.evening: Premium spa evening at the resort — full body aromatherapy massage, deep tissue treatment, and Himalayan salt scrub to restore muscles after the trek. Private fine dining dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — a celebratory multi-course meal with wine pairing to mark the completion of the Annapurna trek.

meals.breakfast: Final trail breakfast at Jhinu Danda — eggs, toast, porridge, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Welcome back lunch at a premium Pokhara lakeside restaurant — fresh grilled fish, salads, and cold pressed juices
meals.dinner: Celebratory 5-course tasting menu at Aegean Bliss Resort — amuse-bouche, Himalayan trout carpaccio, wild mushroom risotto, herb-crusted lamb rack, and chocolate fondant with premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Welcome back to luxury! After 9 days of teahouse trekking, the resort will feel extraordinarily comfortable. The spa team will have been briefed to focus on muscle recovery treatments. Your concierge will have a congratulatory gift and personalized trek completion certificate waiting in your suite.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort — sleep in, enjoy a lavish breakfast on your private terrace overlooking the Annapurna range. Morning guided nature walk through the Pokhara Valley with a local naturalist — explore the subtropical forests, waterfalls, and diverse birdlife of the region. Visit the stunning Davis Falls and Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara — the finest mountain museum in Asia, celebrating the history of Himalayan exploration, the cultures of mountain peoples, and the ecology of the Himalayas. Followed by a curated shopping experience in Pokhara's premium boutiques for authentic Nepali handicrafts, Thangka paintings, and pashmina products with your guide's expert curation.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset paragliding over Pokhara and Phewa Lake (weather permitting) — a tandem flight with a certified instructor offering breathtaking aerial views of the Annapurna range at golden hour. Return to resort for a relaxed private dinner on your beachfront terrace under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Lavish resort breakfast on private terrace — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, seasonal fruits, fresh juices, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a Pokhara lakeside restaurant — wood-fired pizza, Caesar salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Private beachfront terrace dinner at resort — seafood platter, grilled vegetables, artisan bread, and a curated dessert selection with champagne

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding from Sarangkot is one of Pokhara's most iconic experiences and is perfectly safe with certified operators. October provides ideal conditions — clear skies and thermal winds. If weather prevents paragliding, an alternative sunset helicopter flight over the Annapurna range can be arranged at premium cost. Confirm with your concierge by noon.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning sunrise viewing from the resort terrace — a private breakfast set up at the water's edge as the Annapurna massif catches the first light of dawn. Morning at leisure for last-minute relaxation, swimming, or a final yoga session. Optional sunrise helicopter flight over Annapurna for an aerial farewell to the mountains (bookable through concierge at premium rate).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-out from Aegean Bliss Resort. Private farewell lunch at the resort's finest table. Transfer to Pokhara Airport or Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu via private luxury vehicle or chartered flight depending on departure itinerary. Final shopping stop in Kathmandu's Thamel district for premium Nepali souvenirs if time permits.
